journey.title: Tab away after typing an unavailable delivery date
journey.goal: Leaving the date field with Tab closes the calendar even when the typed date is outside the delivery window

steps.title: Type a date outside the delivery window

functionalJourney.title: Move the delivery into June with the pointer
functionalJourney.goal: Clicking through the calendar to June and choosing a day fills the delivery date

guards.title: Type a valid delivery date and Tab away
guards.goal: A correctly typed date is committed and the calendar closes when the user tabs away

plan.root_cause: The datepicker does not hide when the input loses focus via Tab navigation, causing the calendar to remain visible after focus moves to another field.
plan.repair_strategy: Add a blur event listener to the date input field that calls datepicker.hide() to close the calendar when the input loses focus.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Keyboard users can navigate away from the date field without leaving the date picker open, ensuring predictable focus management and visibility of UI components, satisfying WCAG 2.1.1 (Keyboard) and 2.4.3 (Focus Order).
functional_risks: Potential premature closure if blur fires unexpectedly (e.g., when a popup steals focus), but the datepicker already handles external clicks via document mousedown listeners.
If the datepicker programmatically shifts focus without blurring, it could hide prematurely; however, typical usage does not involve such patterns.
verification_requirements: After typing a date and pressing Tab, the date picker (.datepicker) must be invisible.
Selecting a date via mouse or keyboard should still update the input field and respect autohide behavior.
Inline datepickers (if any) must remain unaffected by the change.
Clicking outside the picker should continue to close it as before.

plan.root_cause: The datepicker does not hide when the input loses focus via Tab navigation because no blur event listener is attached to the input field. The previous attempt added a blur listener but incorrectly called `this.hide()` (which doesn't exist on Datepicker) instead of `this.picker.hide()`.
plan.repair_strategy: Add a blur event listener to the date input field that calls `this.picker.hide()` for non-inline datepickers, ensuring the calendar closes when focus moves away via Tab key.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Keyboard users can navigate away from the date field using Tab without leaving the date picker open, ensuring predictable focus management and visibility of UI components, satisfying WCAG 2.1.1 (Keyboard) and 2.4.3 (Focus Order).
functional_risks: Potential premature closure if blur fires unexpectedly (e.g., when a popup steals focus), but the datepicker already handles external clicks via document mousedown listeners.
If the datepicker programmatically shifts focus without blurring, it could hide prematurely; however, typical usage does not involve such patterns.
verification_requirements: After typing a date and pressing Tab, the date picker (.datepicker) must be invisible.
Selecting a date via mouse or keyboard should still update the input field and respect autohide behavior.
Inline datepickers (if any) must remain unaffected by the change.
Clicking outside the picker should continue to close it as before.
Typing an invalid date and pressing Tab should revert the input to the previous valid date and close the picker.
